title: Introduce circuit-breaker retry profiles, typed streaming cursors, and synchronized SDK version bumps
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Several customer workloads and internal benchmarks highlighted tail latency spikes during transient infra failures and long-running streaming sessions where retries either overloaded the service or silently dropped progress. This PR delivers three coordinated pieces: 1) circuit-breaker-aware retry profiles exposed in SDKs to prevent aggressive retries during service degradation; 2) a small, typed streaming cursor API across Python/TS/Go that exposes backpressure hints and a lightweight resume token for more ergonomic consumer code; 3) synchronized version bumps for the three SDKs and release packaging. The change is intentionally cross-repo in scope but implemented from the monorepo to guarantee parity and simultaneous rollout.

What changed (summary):
- Added new retry profile presets and a pluggable CircuitBreakerPolicy interface to all SDK clients. Defaults: conservative, balanced, aggressive. CircuitBreakerPolicy exposes state() and mark_failure()/mark_success() hooks used by the SDK retry loop to short-circuit attempts when error budgets are exhausted.
- Introduced TypedStreamCursor abstraction: Python exposes AsyncTypedCursor with peek_backpressure(), get_resume_token(); TypeScript adds AsyncTypedCursor<T> with peekBackpressure(): number and resumeToken(); Go adds TypedCursor with PeekBackpressure() int and ResumeToken() string. These are intentionally minimal to keep cross-language ergonomics tight.
- Exposed a new ClientOptions.circuit_breaker in each SDK and a top-level env flag REDWOOD_SDK_CB_DISABLED for testing/rollouts.
- API/Behavior parity fixes: unified transient error classification (RetryableTransientError) and mapped HTTP/HTTP2 and websocket error families to the same retry decider across SDKs.
- Developer ergonomics improvements: Python contextmanager now supports 'with client.session(timeout=...)' returning an AsyncTypedCursor; TypeScript iterator helpers include tryNext() which returns {value, done, resumeToken}. Go stream handle adds ResumeTo(token) convenience method.
- Packaging: bump python -> 1.12.0, typescript -> 2.4.0, go -> 0.9.0; changelogs updated.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc linked (ENG-4521)
- [x] Unit tests for retry logic and circuit-breaker state machine
- [x] Integration test: streaming resume round-trip (CI job)
- [x] Cross-SDK lint and type checks
- [x] Release notes prepared

Commits (high level):
- feat(retry): add CircuitBreakerPolicy and conservative/balanced/aggressive presets
- feat(stream): introduce TypedStreamCursor across py/ts/go with backpressure hint
- fix(errors): unify RetryableTransientError mapping across SDKs
- perf(telemetry): sample cb state transitions for high-cardinality tracing off by default
- chore(release): bump versions and update changelogs

Testing notes: Local integration harness (benchmark-lab) validated that the conservative profile reduced retry amplification during simulated DB-step failures by ~82% and kept tail latency bounded. Streaming resume tests were run over websocket and HTTP2 adapters; small differences in token encoding handled at the SDK boundary.

Risk and rollout: This is non-breaking by default (circuit breaker is opt-in via ClientOptions; default profiles are safe). We coordinated simultaneous release across SDKs to avoid client-server mismatch for resume tokens and error classes. For immediate mitigation during rollout we included REDWOOD_SDK_CB_DISABLED to disable CB checks in emergencies.

Related work: ENG-4521, ENG-4530, PM-1293. See design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4521/circuit-breaker-and-typed-streams

Merge notes: squash merge used to keep history compact. Post-merge: create packaged releases and publish to PyPI/NPM/go modules and update example quickstarts in redwood-quickstarts repo.
release_notes: Added circuit-breaker-aware retry profiles (conservative/balanced/aggressive), typed streaming cursor APIs with backpressure hints and resume tokens across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. SDK versions bumped: py@1.12.0, ts@2.4.0, go@0.9.0. Improved retry/error classification to ensure parity across SDKs. Non-breaking defaults and rollout controls provided.
review_thread: Daniel Ortega: Can we expose circuit-breaker metrics at the client level (counters/gauge) so customers can alert on CB trips?
Maya Chen: Added cb.transition_count and cb_state gauge in telemetry; gated by ClientOptions.telemetry_sampling to avoid high-cardinality by default.
Priya Nair: The TypeScript peekBackpressure numbers need clearer units in docs (is this bytes or events?).
Maya Chen: Clarified in docs and added docstring: peekBackpressure returns approximate queued tokens (events) for consumer backpressure decisions.
Liam O'Connor: Go ResumeTo semantics looked racy when combined with concurrent Resume calls. Can you add a small mutex around state updates?
Maya Chen: Added mutex and added deterministic unit test that simulated concurrent resumes; pushed fix in second commit.
commits: feat(stream): typed cursor API for cross-lang parity
test: add integration tests for streaming resume
chore(release): bump sdk versions and update changelogs
